Could you list every single concert on Taylor Swift’s official tour from January 1, 2010, to May 1, 2025, including the specific date, the concert’s English name, the country, the city, and the venue. Each show should be on its own line, in chronological order from earliest to latest.

Please organize the results in one Markdown table with the following columns:
Date, the Concert’s English Name,  Host Country,  Host City, Host Venue

Don't ask me any questions, just output the results according to the columns without omitting cells arbitrarily. The output format is a markdown code block.

### Output Requirements
- **Format**: Markdown table wrapped in triple backticks with markdown specifier
- **Required Columns** (5): date, theconcert’senglishname, hostcountry, hostcity, hostvenue
- **Unique Key Columns**: date
- **Expected Rows**: 534 rows

**IMPORTANT**: Write the markdown table to `answer.txt` in the workspace.

**IMPORTANT**: You must NOT read the `ground_truth.csv` file in the workspace. Use web search to find all information.

**Note**: You may use available tools or skills in the system to complete this task.

and you need to complete the task in 480s.

2009 was Taylor Swift’s year, but someone forgot to tell the Fearless One that was it. She keeps going strong.

[Return to the current calendar](https://theswiftagency.com/calendar)

January

- January 19: Digital release of Today Was A Fairytale on iTunes.

- January 22: Hope for Haiti Telethon on all major networks at 8pm EST. Taylor will be performing live.

- January 27: Taylor will perform at  Unforgettable Evening event in LA, benefiting the EIF’s Women’s Cancer Research Fund.

- January 28: CBS re-runs the CSI episode with Taylor Swift. 9PM ET.

- January 29: She makes an appearance in the Early Show in CBS at 7AM ET.

- January 31: 52nd Grammy Awards in Los Angeles, California. It will be broadcasted on CBS, 8pm -11:30pm ET/PT. Taylor is nominated for 8 awards and scheduled to perform. She won 4: Best Country Song, Best Female Country Vocal, Best Country Album and Album of the Year 🙂

February

- February 4: The Fearless Tour 2010 begins with the Australian tour in Brisbane, Queensland.

- February 6: Australian tour concert in Sydney, New South Wales.

- February 7: Australian tour concert in Sydney, New South Wales.

- February 8: Australian tour concert in Newcastle, New South Wales.

- February 9: Release of the Valentine’s Day movie soundtrack in stores and online.

- February 10: Australian tour concert in Melbourne, Victoria.

- February 11: Australian tour concert in Melbourne, Victoria.

- February 12: Last concert of the Australian tour in Adelaide, Australia.

- February 12: Valentine’s Day movie opens.

- February 16: The 2010 Brit Awards in London, England.

- February 17: First ever Japan tour concert in Tokyo, Japan.

- February 26: [Caitlin Evanson](https://theswiftagency.wordpress.com/2009/11/15/caitlin-evanson/)‘s Birthday

March

Update! Voting is now closed.

- November 24: Taylor Swift’s performance of Back To December will air on The Ellen Degeneres Show. Check your local TV listings.

- November 24: Taylor Swift will appear on the Chelsea Lately show. Check your local TV listings.

The special airs on [NBC](http://www.nbc.com/) at 8PM Eastern Time.

[Vote vote vote](http://theacas.com/vote-artistawards.php)!

Taylor is up for Artist of the Year, Female Artist of the Year and Touring Artist of the Year. You can vote at [theacas.com](http://theacas.com/vote-artistawards.php). Taylor is up for Artist of the Year: Female and Touring Artist of the Year. [Vote vote vote](http://theacas.com/vote-artistawards.php)!

- December 10: The concert dates of August 27 and 28 in Los Angeles, CA at the Staples Center are on sale to the general public on [Ticketmaster](http://www.ticketmaster.com/search?q=taylor+swift) at 10:00am.

- December 12: The Hub will rerun their Taylor Swift special Journey To Fearless.

- December 13: Taylor Swift turns 21 years old 🙂

Several fan activities will happen during the day, including an acoustic performance at 2pm. More details at [TaylorSwift.com](http://www.taylorswift.com/13-hour).

- June 17: Songwriters Hall of Fame. Taylor Swift receives the Hal David Starlight Award.

- June 19: Atlantis, Bahamas. She performs at the Imperial Ballroom.

- June 22: Nashville Raising: A Benefit Concert for Flood Recovery headed by Tim McGraw and Faith Hill. Taylor Swift is in the line-up.

July

- July 10: Taylor Swift performs at  the [Cavendish Beach Music Festival](http://www.cavendishbeachmusic.com/) in Cavendish, Prince Edward Island, Canada. Another Fearless Evening.

- July 20: Taylor Swift chats live with fans about her new album via [Ustream.tv](http://www.ustream.tv/user/TaylorSwift) at 4pm Central Daylight Time.

August

- August 4: After a leak, [Big Machine Records](http://www.bigmachinerecords.com/index.cfm?id=6&viewStory=411) jump starts the release of the first new single, Mine. Now available on [iTunes](http://itunes.apple.com/us/album/mine-single/id385990165)!

- August 7: Taylor Swift performs at the [Summer Sonic](http://www.summersonic.com/2010/tickets/) Festival in Osaka, Japan.

- August 8: Taylor Swift performs at the [Summer Sonic](http://www.summersonic.com/2010/tickets/) Festival in Tokio, Japan.

- August 9: [Teen Choice Awards](http://www.teenchoiceawards.com/index.php) in Los Angeles. Taylor Swift wins Choice Music Female Country Artist, Choice Country Album for Fearless, Choice Country song for Fifteen and Choice Movie Breakout Female for Valentine’s Day.

- August 16: The new single, Mine, from the third album, Speak Now is released on radio stations. Available now on [iTunes](http://www.bigmachinerecords.com/index.cfm?id=6&viewStory=411)!

- August 19: Pre-order Speak Now at [www.SpeakNow13.com](http://www.speaknow13.com).

- August 25: Voting closes for the VMAs!

- August 27: Mine will get its video premiere on CMT at 8pm ET/5PM PT. It will be a LIVE half-hour special event.

- August 31: The first batch of CMA nominations are announced at the Ryman Auditorium in Nashville, TN by Justin Moore and Chris Young.

September

- September 1: The remaining categories of the CMA nominations are announced by Miranda Lambert and Dierks Bentley on Good Morning America.

- September 1: [CMA Music Festival: Country’s Night To Rock](http://www.cmafest.com/) airs on ABC at 8/7c.

- September 9: Taylor Swift will perform at kickoff time in New Orleans for the Saints vs. Vikings game to be broadcast on NBC at 7:30pm ET.

- September 12: [MTV Video Music Awards](http://www.mtv.com/ontv/vma/2010/) airs on MTV at 9/8c. Taylor Swift was nominated for Female Video of the Year for Fifteen. Lady Gaga won it. Taylor performs Innocent for the first time ever, a song dedicated to the previous VMA incident and forgiveness.

- September 18: Tickets go on sale for the [44th CMA Awards](http://www.cmaawards.com/), which takes place November 10.

- September 21: Voting period ends for [J-14 Teen Icon Awards](http://www.j-14.com/2010/09/introducing-j-14s-teen-icon-awards-official-nominations.html).

- September 22: Voting period ends for the [Country Weekly](http://www.countryweekly.com/sexiest_2010/vote/surveys/723) most beautiful woman in country music.

- September 23: Taylor Swift performs at the [All For The Hall fundraiser at Club Nokia](http://www.clubnokia.com/eventdetail.php?id=28714), Los Angeles that benefits the Country Music Hall of Fame and Museum.

- September 27: Taylor Swift visits Milan, Italy.

- September 28: She is scheduled to perform on X-Factor Italy.

- September 29: She attends Roberto Cavalli’s 40th Anniversary gala dinner and party at Ecole Superiure des Beaux Arts in Paris, France.

- September 30: Taylor Swift is scheduled for an interview at [NRJ](http://www.nrj.fr/music-509/exclus-nrj-526/article/249731-taylor-swift-en-interview-dans-le-6-9-gagne-tes-places-.html) in Paris, France. You can [enter the contest](http://www.nrj.fr/music-509/exclus-nrj-526/article/249731-taylor-swift-en-interview-dans-le-6-9-gagne-tes-places-.html) to be part of the audience.

October

- October 1: CMT’s [Speak Now with Taylor Swift in New York City](http://winwithtaylor.com/) contest registration closes.

- October 4:Speak Now will get a 30-second preview on Comcast On Demand and [XfinityTv.com](http://www.xfinitytv.com/) starting one minute past midnight. E! News will show a clip and interview in the evening.

- October 5:Speak Now goes on sale on iTunes.

- October 9: Taylor Swift performs at the [Grand Ole Opry](http://search2.opry.com/?view=events&q=Taylor)! Dolly Parton performs on the very same night! [Get your tickets now](http://search2.opry.com/?view=events&q=Taylor).

- October 11:Back To December will get a 30-second preview on Comcast On Demand and [XfinityTv.com](http://www.xfinitytv.com/) starting one minute past midnight. E! News will show a clip and interview in the evening.

- October 12:Back To December goes on sale on iTunes. The Glamour magazine with Taylor Swift’s interview, photoshoot and cover comes out in newsstands.

- October 18:Mean will get a 30-second preview on Comcast On Demand and [XfinityTv.com](http://www.xfinitytv.com/) starting one minute past midnight. E! News will show a clip and interview in the evening.

- October 18: Taylor Swift performs in a private concert at a secret location in Paris! Promoted by [Goom Radio](http://www.goomradio.fr/#page=radio/just-hits/2010/10/07/taylor-swift-en-showcase--gagne-tes-invits).

- October 18: Royal Caribbean International launches its contest [The Allure of Taylor Swift](http://theallureoftaylor.com/#). You win a 7-night cruise for two on the Bahamas including two tickets for Taylor’s on board concert. The promotion period starts now and runs until October 29. The cruise dates are tentatively scheduled for January 16-23, 2011. Sorry, only US residents eligible.

- October 19:Mean goes on sale on iTunes.

- October 22: The ticket sales for the UK concerts on March 22, 29 and 30 of 2011 open on [SeeTickets](http://www2.seetickets.com/see/event.asp?artist=TAYLOR+SWIFT). [Play.com](http://www.play.com/Music/CD/4-/15957600/Speak-Now/Product.html) will give you a ticket pre-sales code if you pre-order the [Speak Now CD](http://www.play.com/Music/CD/4-/15957600/Speak-Now/Product.html) or [Speak Now Deluxe Edition CD](http://www.play.com/Music/CD/4-/16686744/Speak-Now/Product.html)! More at [Play.com](http://www.play.com/Music/CD/4-/15957600/Speak-Now/Product.html).

- October 22: Taylor Swift appears on [Paul O’Grady Live](http://www.itv.com/paulogrady) in London, England.

- October 22, 23 and 24: Taylor Swift’s Journey To Fearless premieres on [The Hub](http://www.hubworld.com/) network.

- October 22: Story Of Us will get a 30-second preview on Comcast On Demand and [XfinityTv.com](http://www.xfinitytv.com/) starting one minute past midnight. E! News will show the clip in the evening.

- October 23: Last chance to send your video entries for the [Team Hug](http://www.teamhug.org/)contest! Closes at 5pm Eastern time.

- October 25: Speak Now WORLDWIDE DATE RELEASE on iTunes and on major music retailers around the world.

- October 25: Tickets go on sale for a lot of tour concert dates! See February and March for ticket links.

- October 25: [103.7 KISS-FM](http://www.1037kissfm.com/) in Milwaukee will be [taken over](http://wxss.taylorswifttakeover.com/) by Taylor Swift at noon.

- October 25: A group of winners of contests held around the world will join Taylor for a private performance at the United Nations in New York City. [Taylor Swift Live Stream from New York City](http://www.cmt.com/shows/events/taylor_swift_live_stream/) will be available on many of MTV Networks’ web properties, including CMT.com, MTV.com, VH1.com and websites across Europe, Asia, Australia and Latin America at 7PM Eastern, 6PM Central. Now also available on [Ustream](http://www.ustream.tv/taylorswift).

- October 25: Taylor Swift takes over [Dial-Global Hot Country Forum](http://www.dial-global.com/index.php?option=com_content&view=article&id=244:taylor-swift-takes-over-dial-globals-hot-country-format&catid=1:on-the-dial-press&Itemid=92) from 8pm to 9pm EST.

- October 26: Taylor will perform live for fans from Rockefeller Plaza on the [Today Show](http://today.msnbc.msn.com/) as part of their fall concert series. Fans can apply for passes to the show at: [http://today.msnbc.msn.com/id/30012397](http://today.msnbc.msn.com/id/30012397) . That night, she will do an interview and performance on the [Late Show with David Letterman](http://www.cbs.com/late_night/late_show/). The [Today Show](http://today.msnbc.msn.com/) airs on NBC from 7:00 – 11:00 a.m. (all time zones), and [Late Show with David Letterman](http://www.cbs.com/late_night/late_show/) airs on CBS at 11:30 p.m. (ET/PT).

- October 27: Taylor’s day starts with [Live! With Regis & Kelly](http://regisandkelly.go.com/) where she will do an interview and performance. The show airs on ABC affiliates nationwide, check for listings by area. That afternoon, she will visit Scholastic’s New York headquarters, where she will take time out from her busy release week schedule for a special literacy event, [Read Now! with Taylor Swift](http://www.scholastic.com/readeveryday/readnow.htm), as part of the company’s 90th Anniversary Literacy campaign ([register here](http://vxlive.feedroom.com/feedroom/http/4000/5172/5174/7045/Lobby/default.htm)). Later in the day, she will visit Madame Tussaud’s New York – the famed Times Square wax attraction — for the unveiling of her original wax figure.

- October 27: Taylor will now be appearing at the JetBlue terminal, Gate 14 (there is no Gate 13, superstitious much?) at Kennedy International Airport in New York City on Wednesday, October 27. Taylor Swift has a chartered flight from New York to Los Angeles with very lucky fans included and even an improvised concert during the flight.

- October 28:[Ellen DeGeneres Show](http://ellen.warnerbros.com/) will celebrate the release of Speak Now by once again devoting an entire hour-long show to throwing Taylor’s official album release party. Participate in Ellen’s [Ultimate Taylor Swift Fan](http://ellen.warnerbros.com/show/respond/?PlugID=463#ixzz12O0vM7jI) contest!

- October 29: Taylor Swift performs at Hollywood and Highland in Los Angeles, California.

- October 29: The Royal Caribbean International contest [The Allure of Taylor Swift](http://theallureoftaylor.com/#) entry period closes. The cruise dates are tentatively scheduled for January 16-23, 2011. Sorry, only US residents eligible.

November

- November 1: The Speak Now Album Release Party will air on the [Ellen DeGeneres Show](http://ellen.warnerbros.com/) on Monday, November 1st (syndicated, check local listings).

- November 2: Taylor will perform on [Dancing With the Stars](http://abc.go.com/shows/dancing-with-the-stars), airing on ABC at 9:00 p.m. (ET/PT).

- November 4: Taylor gets interviewed on CTV’s Canada AM. Enter 99.9FM’s [contest to be in the audience](http://toronto.virginradio.ca/Channels/listentowin/Story.aspx?ID=1303207)!

- November 4: Taylor Swift will be at the [MuchMusic](http://blog.muchmusic.com/taylor-swift-is-coming-to-muchmusic/) building in Toronto, Canada at 5pm Eastern time.

- November 9: The [BMI Awards](http://www.bmi.com/press/entry/548690).

- November 10: The 44th Annual [CMA Awards](http://www.cmaawards.com/) ceremony takes place live from the Bridgestone Arena in Nashville, TN. The event airs on ABC at 8/7c. Taylor Swift is nominated for Female Vocalist of the Year. She also is scheduled to perform. Update: She lost to Miranda Lambert.

- November 11: The CMA Country Christmas is taped. Taylor is not scheduled to appear but it’s still a major Country Music show.

- November 14: Taylor is scheduled to perform at the [BBC Radio 1’s Teen Awards](http://www.bbc.co.uk/radio1/teenawards/2010/about/).

- November 16: Speak Now is released on vinyl.

- November 17: TV appearance on [Fuji TV/SmapXSmap Japan TV](http://www.fujitv.co.jp/en/).

- November 18: TV appearance on [Nippon TV/Zoom In Japan TV](http://www.ntv.co.jp/english/).

- November 21: The [American Music Awards](http://abc.go.com/shows/american-music-awards) are broadcast live on ABC at 8pm Eastern time. The winners will be decided via online voting through [ABC.com](http://www.ama.abc.com/) and [AMAvote.com](http://www.amavote.com/). Taylor Swift is nominated for Favorite Female Country Artist. Update! Voting is now closed.

- November 22: Taylor Swift will appear on the Tonight Show with Jay Leno. Check your local TV listings.

- November 24: Taylor Swift’s performance of Back To December will air on The Ellen Degeneres Show. Check your local TV listings.

- November 24: Taylor Swift will appear on the Chelsea Lately show. Check your local TV listings.

- November 25: “Taylor Swift – Speak Now” will document the days of the Speak Now album release including a trip from New York City to Los Angeles, her multiple performances, behind the scenes footage and her concert 30,000 feet in the air on a plane ride across the country. The special airs on [NBC](http://www.nbc.com/) at 8PM Eastern Time.

December

- December 1: [E! Entertainment Special](http://www.eonline.com) on Taylor Swift at 10pm Eastern time.

- December 3: Atlanta, Los Angeles, San Jose, Sacramento and Toronto are on sale to the general public on [Ticketmaster](http://www.ticketmaster.com/search?q=taylor+swift) at 10:00am.

- December 3: The first ever [CMT Artists of the Year](http://www.cmt.com/shows/events/artists-of-the-year/index.jhtml) airing Dec. 3 at 8/7c on CMT. Taylor Swift is among the honored ones.

- December 4: Foxborough is on sale to the general public on [Ticketmaster](http://www.ticketmaster.com/search?q=taylor+swift) at 10:00am. Montreal is on sale at [Evenko](http://www.evenko.ca/en/show/event/taylor-swift-4842).

- December 4: The voting for the [American Country Awards](http://theacas.com/vote-artistawards.php) closes. You can vote at [theacas.com](http://theacas.com/vote-artistawards.php). Taylor is up for Artist of the Year: Female and Touring Artist of the Year. [Vote vote vote](http://theacas.com/vote-artistawards.php)!

- December 6: The first ever [American Country Awards](http://theacas.com/vote-artistawards.php) show will air on the Fox Network. Taylor is up for Artist of the Year, Female Artist of the Year and Touring Artist of the Year. You can vote at [theacas.com](http://theacas.com/vote-artistawards.php). Taylor is up for Artist of the Year: Female and Touring Artist of the Year. [Vote vote vote](http://theacas.com/vote-artistawards.php)!

- December 10: The concert dates of August 27 and 28 in Los Angeles, CA at the Staples Center are on sale to the general public on [Ticketmaster](http://www.ticketmaster.com/search?q=taylor+swift) at 10:00am.

- December 12: The Hub will rerun their Taylor Swift special Journey To Fearless.

- December 13: Taylor Swift turns 21 years old 🙂

[Return to the current calendar](https://theswiftagency.com/calendar)

(Sources: [TaylorSwift.com](http://www.taylorswift.com), and way too many to enumerate!)

#### 2013-2014

 “The RED Tour” was Taylor’s third concert tour. Launched in support of her fourth studio album, [RED](https://taylorswiftswitzerland.ch/index.php/albums/red-album/) (2012), the tour began on March 13, 2013 in Omaha, Nebraska, and concluded on June 12, 2014 in Singapore. It became the highest-grossing tour by a country artist in history, bringing in an overall gross of $150 million.

 Seeing Taylor live in 2013 was seeing a maestro at the top of her or anyone’s game. “The RED Tour” was flashy, incorporated circus elements and took full advantage of the stadiums that had now become the norm for her concerts. Hipster costumes, advanced pyrotechnics, and plenty of fan interaction set her third major tour apart from her previous concerts. RED was also not only the title of her current album and show, it was the predominant color scheme favored by Taylor for her double-storey stage, the visuals and videos on her giant LED screen backdrop and multiple costume changes. The red sequins on her guitar matched the ones on her microphone, her shoes and 80 percent of the crowd.

##### Table of Contents

### Background and Development

 While she was immersed in promotional appearances for her new album, Taylor was already hatching plans for the concert tour. On October 25, 2012, in partnership with ABC News on the prime-time TV special “All Access Nashville with Katie Couric — A Special Edition of 20/20”, she announced that she would launch a North American stadium and arena tour in early 2013 in support of RED. “Of course, you know the tour will be a big representation of this record,” Taylor later told Billboard. “I’m so excited to see what songs the fans like the most and which ones jump to the forefront, because that’s the first step. We always see which songs are really the passionate songs and the ones the fans are freaking out over the most, and those are the ones that are definitely in the set list. I can’t wait for that.” She also teased that “The RED Tour” would look a lot different than her previous concert tours, the “[Fearless Tour](https://taylorswiftswitzerland.ch/index.php/tours/fearless-tour/)” (2009-2010) and the “[Speak Now World Tour](https://taylorswiftswitzerland.ch/index.php/tours/speak-now-world-tour/)” (2011-2012):

 «The visuals portrayed on this tour will be, I guess, more grown-up and a little bit more mature than things we’ve done in the past. I think on my previous albums and my previous tours, I’ve really liked to operate in the element of fantasy, and I think that this tour incorporates a little bit more reality into the visuals, which is nice.»

 Taylor Swift

 Tickets began going on sale Nov. 16 for Taylor’s original 58-date trek, which would be stopping at mostly arenas and nine stadiums. It was also announced that up-and-coming British singer-songwroter Ed Sheeran, who guests on the RED track “[Everything Has Changed](https://taylorswiftswitzerland.ch/index.php/albums/red-album/red-songs/everything-has-changed/),” would be the main opening act for the North American  leg of the tour.

### The Show

 The audience was an important part of the show on “The RED Tour,” with their homemade red costumes, placards, Lite Brite codes and so many glowsticks that Taylor decided to just gift everyone in the audience a glowing wristband, come [next tour](https://taylorswiftswitzerland.ch/index.php/tours/1989-world-tour/). Seeing Taylor onstage during “The RED Tour” was witnessing a level of total commitment, total fan fervor, total connection between audience and performer. No other pop auteur could touch her for emotional excess or musical reach. By this point in her career, she was “feelin’ 22,” and made her growth clear by entering the stage to Lenny Kravitz’s “American Woman” (having previously used Tom Petty’s “[American Girl](https://taylorswiftswitzerland.ch/index.php/standalone-singles/american-girl/)”). Taylor was a true arena-rock goddess at an amazing peak.

Once the lights went out, the screaming never flagged, and neither did the star. Drums started to play, a guitar solo kicked in and Taylor’s giant silhouette appeared on a red curtain. When it dropped for the first chorus of “[State of Grace](https://taylorswiftswitzerland.ch/index.php/albums/red-album/red-songs/state-of-grace/),” she appeared, wearing a black hat, white lacey top, black leather shorts and sparkling, sequined ruby red oxford shoes, smiling, wide-eyed and full of wonder. As the ceiling over the stage exploded in a cascade of sparks, she took in the view of the crowd with amazement, even though she long ago sold out her first stadium.

It soon turned out that every song was its own mini-show. The impressive production techniques continued with Taylor grabbing a fluorescent, flashing drum to beat in the dark during the second song, the fan-favorite “[Holy Ground](https://taylorswiftswitzerland.ch/index.php/albums/red-album/red-songs/holy-ground/).” 12 other drummers leaped between floor and ceiling, bouncing on harnesses as they pounded along.

 Nobody could touch Taylor for fan hysteria, either. After darting around the stage for the first few minutes of the show, she made the first of a number of heartfelt speeches to her adoring crowd. “Hi, I’m Taylor,” she said by way of an introduction to the sound of thousands of screaming fans. “I write songs about my feelings. I’m told I have a lot of feelings.” She then gently warned the audience to “expect the unexpected” before topping off the opening segment with a rendition of “[Red](https://taylorswiftswitzerland.ch/index.php/albums/red-album/red-songs/red-song/),” complete with an impressive flag-waving gymnastic routine from her dancers. A quick costume change and she returned with her early hit “[You Belong With Me](https://taylorswiftswitzerland.ch/index.php/albums/fearless-album/fearless-songs/you-belong-with-me/)” before a set change to recall a bygone Hollywood era for “[The Lucky One](https://taylorswiftswitzerland.ch/index.php/albums/red-album/red-songs/the-lucky-one/).”

Through her eight wardrobe changes during the show, Taylor added many other set design changes, which was meant to take fans through the story of her songs. In fact, she spent quite a bit of time talking to the audience. Before “[Mean](https://taylorswiftswitzerland.ch/index.php/albums/speak-now-album/speak-now-songs/mean/)” she spoke about bullying and how she vowed to never be mean to anyone on purpose after she was treated poorly in school as a child. On a brighter note, she championed the good parts of a past relationship with an upbeat mashup of her own “[Stay Stay Stay](https://taylorswiftswitzerland.ch/index.php/albums/red-album/red-songs/stay-stay-stay/)“ and The Lumineers’ “Ho Hey.”

The mechanics of the show involved everyone. There was an inner pit, where fans could stand in between the catwalks which jutted out of the stage. Those seats were only made available to members of her official fan club, but Taylor also had a B-stage at the back of the floor seating area where she performed a few songs. Her most recent hit, “[22](https://taylorswiftswitzerland.ch/index.php/albums/red-album/red-songs/22-2/),” sent her around the side of the arena floor, through the screaming crowd, along with her dancers, to the small stage at the rear. She touched as many waving hands as she could along the way, singing all the while. It is a signature move of Taylor’s, to perform specially for the back of the stadium, and she exceeded expectations this time. Sitting on her sparkly red stool, playing acoustic guitar, the second stage rose high into the arena, and revolved, as she first sang a secret surprise song, then duetted with Ed Sheeran for “Everything Has Changed” and finally performed the ballad “[Begin Again](https://taylorswiftswitzerland.ch/index.php/albums/red-album/red-songs/begin-again/).” Then she launched into “[Sparks Fly](https://taylorswiftswitzerland.ch/index.php/albums/speak-now-album/speak-now-songs/sparks-fly/)” and flew over the audience back to the main stage just in time for more fireworks.

Her final five tracks provided even more highlights. Arguably the best moment of the night was the double-shot of “[I Knew You Were Trouble.](https://taylorswiftswitzerland.ch/index.php/albums/red-album/red-songs/i-knew-you-were-trouble/)” into “[All Too Well](https://taylorswiftswitzerland.ch/index.php/albums/red-album/red-songs/all-too-well/).” Taylor turned “Trouble” into a blast of razzle-dazzle choreography in fancy-dress masquerade-ball mode. Then she sat alone to play “All Too Well,” her most majestic ballad. “So this happened to me one time and I knew that in order to get past it I needed to write about it,” she said before the song. “So instead of trying to write how I felt about it, I just decided that it might be better to just write about what happened, because I remembered everything.” It was just her and her piano and several thousand other girls singing along. It was the highlight of a show that was nothing but highlights.

“[Love Story](https://taylorswiftswitzerland.ch/index.php/albums/fearless-album/fearless-songs/love-story/)” and “[Treacherous](https://taylorswiftswitzerland.ch/index.php/albums/red-album/red-songs/treacherous/)” followed, complete with a music box theme and an (almost) Cirque Du Soleil inspired routine with the dancers performing as wind-up ballerinas. Finally, the finale was truly outstanding. It was like Alice and Wonderland had wandered into a circus tent, with rabbits and stilt-walkers everywhere, and Taylor was their ring-leader in a red sequinned coat and top hat, clearly loving every sly moment of “[We Are Never Ever Getting Back Together](https://taylorswiftswitzerland.ch/index.php/albums/red-album/red-songs/we-are-never-ever-getting-back-together/).” The catwalk lifted up and spun her out across the audience, as heart-shaped red confetti canons exploded, and she led everyone in a deafening sing along, before saying thank you, good night, and disappearing back under the stage. There was no need for an encore — fans had already gotten everything they came for and more.

### Secret Song

 Every night, Taylor would sing a secret song — an acoustic version of one of her old songs. Fans could suggest songs online through Twitter and Facebook and Taylor would sing the most requested one. Sometimes she also performed a song that a fan from the pre-show Meet & Greet wanted to hear.

### Surprise Guests

 A fan of the concert cameo, Taylor welcomed many special surprise guests to her tour. Highlights include Carly Simon, who performed her classic hit “You’re So Vain” with Taylor at Gillette Stadium, Fall Out Boy, who appeared to sing “My Songs Know What You Did in the Dark,” and Jennifer Lopez, who brought the house down at Staples Center with “Jenny from the Block.”

### The RED Tour Movie

 The “Red Tour” remains Taylor’s only concert tour to never have been filmed. According to the CEO of her former label [Big Machine](https://taylorswiftswitzerland.ch/index.php/wiki/big-machine-records/), Scott Borchetta, he and the management never planned to film the concert or to put it on DVD. He said Taylor also never insisted to film “The RED Tour” due to her process of switching genres. Rumours online suggest that there was in fact a concert film in the works, but some serious allegations regarding the director got revealed at the time — which is why the project was permanently scrapped.

### Club RED

 Club RED was the name of the VIP backstage meet and greet for “The RED Tour.” As they did on Taylor’s previous tours, her mother, [Andrea Swift](https://taylorswiftswitzerland.ch/index.php/wiki/family/andrea-swift/), and members of [Taylor Nation](https://taylorswiftswitzerland.ch/index.php/wiki/13-management/) hand-picked fans that stood out the most during the concert: they had spent the entire concert screaming, crying, and bobbing mega-size [Meredith](https://taylorswiftswitzerland.ch/index.php/wiki/cats/meredith-grey/) cat heads in the crowd hoping to get picked by Taylor’s team to go to the exclusive event. The setup for Club RED included a bar, fridges stacked with [Diet Cokes](https://taylorswiftswitzerland.ch/index.php/wiki/brand-deals/diet-coke/) (a nod to the main sponsor of the tour), dining booths, sleek silver and red décor, a photobooth and lots of free food, including pizza. Once Taylor showed up, she would chat with every fan in the room, sign one of their belongings, and take a picture with them.

### Critical Reception

 “The RED Tour” received positive reviews from music critics, with many citing Taylor’s atmospheric performances as a specific area of praise. Writing for Rolling Stone, Rob Sheffield praised her “emotional excess [and] musical reach”, while Rebbeca Nicholson of The Guardian gave a 5-star review, stating Taylor was “staggeringly nice” and a “consummate crowd pleaser”. Digital Spy contributor Emma Dibdin stated the tour combined “whimsical spectacle with Swift’s trademark emotional intimacy,” and that it “capitalises on exactly what makes Swift such a powerful figure for her audience, the sincere blend of aspirational and relatable.”

### Records

 Taylor became the first solo female artist in 20 years to headline a national stadium tour through Australia, with the last being Madonna’s “The Girlie Show World Tour” in 1993. Taylor performed to a crowd of over 40,900 fans at the Allianz Stadium in Sydney, Australia, becoming the first female artist in history to sell out the stadium since it was opened in 1988.

“The RED Tour” also became the highest-grossing tour by a country artist in history, bringing in an overall gross of $150 million surpassing the prior country artist record held by double-billed Tim McGraw and Faith Hill “Soul2Soul II Tour” that brought in $141 million.

#### 2013-2014

 “The RED Tour” was Taylor’s third concert tour. Launched in support of her fourth studio album, [RED](https://taylorswiftswitzerland.ch/index.php/albums/red-album/) (2012), the tour began on March 13, 2013 in Omaha, Nebraska, and concluded on June 12, 2014 in Singapore. It became the highest-grossing tour by a country artist in history, bringing in an overall gross of $150 million.

 Seeing Taylor live in 2013 was seeing a maestro at the top of her or anyone’s game. “The RED Tour” was flashy, incorporated circus elements and took full advantage of the stadiums that had now become the norm for her concerts. Hipster costumes, advanced pyrotechnics, and plenty of fan interaction set her third major tour apart from her previous concerts. RED was also not only the title of her current album and show, it was the predominant color scheme favored by Taylor for her double-storey stage, the visuals and videos on her giant LED screen backdrop and multiple costume changes. The red sequins on her guitar matched the ones on her microphone, her shoes and 80 percent of the crowd.

##### Table of Contents

### Background and Development

 While she was immersed in promotional appearances for her new album, Taylor was already hatching plans for the concert tour. On October 25, 2012, in partnership with ABC News on the prime-time TV special “All Access Nashville with Katie Couric — A Special Edition of 20/20”, she announced that she would launch a North American stadium and arena tour in early 2013 in support of RED. “Of course, you know the tour will be a big representation of this record,” Taylor later told Billboard. “I’m so excited to see what songs the fans like the most and which ones jump to the forefront, because that’s the first step. We always see which songs are really the passionate songs and the ones the fans are freaking out over the most, and those are the ones that are definitely in the set list. I can’t wait for that.” She also teased that “The RED Tour” would look a lot different than her previous concert tours, the “[Fearless Tour](https://taylorswiftswitzerland.ch/index.php/tours/fearless-tour/)” (2009-2010) and the “[Speak Now World Tour](https://taylorswiftswitzerland.ch/index.php/tours/speak-now-world-tour/)” (2011-2012):

 «The visuals portrayed on this tour will be, I guess, more grown-up and a little bit more mature than things we’ve done in the past. I think on my previous albums and my previous tours, I’ve really liked to operate in the element of fantasy, and I think that this tour incorporates a little bit more reality into the visuals, which is nice.»

 Taylor Swift

 Tickets began going on sale Nov. 16 for Taylor’s original 58-date trek, which would be stopping at mostly arenas and nine stadiums. It was also announced that up-and-coming British singer-songwroter Ed Sheeran, who guests on the RED track “[Everything Has Changed](https://taylorswiftswitzerland.ch/index.php/albums/red-album/red-songs/everything-has-changed/),” would be the main opening act for the North American  leg of the tour.

### The Show

 The audience was an important part of the show on “The RED Tour,” with their homemade red costumes, placards, Lite Brite codes and so many glowsticks that Taylor decided to just gift everyone in the audience a glowing wristband, come [next tour](https://taylorswiftswitzerland.ch/index.php/tours/1989-world-tour/). Seeing Taylor onstage during “The RED Tour” was witnessing a level of total commitment, total fan fervor, total connection between audience and performer. No other pop auteur could touch her for emotional excess or musical reach. By this point in her career, she was “feelin’ 22,” and made her growth clear by entering the stage to Lenny Kravitz’s “American Woman” (having previously used Tom Petty’s “[American Girl](https://taylorswiftswitzerland.ch/index.php/standalone-singles/american-girl/)”). Taylor was a true arena-rock goddess at an amazing peak.

Once the lights went out, the screaming never flagged, and neither did the star. Drums started to play, a guitar solo kicked in and Taylor’s giant silhouette appeared on a red curtain. When it dropped for the first chorus of “[State of Grace](https://taylorswiftswitzerland.ch/index.php/albums/red-album/red-songs/state-of-grace/),” she appeared, wearing a black hat, white lacey top, black leather shorts and sparkling, sequined ruby red oxford shoes, smiling, wide-eyed and full of wonder. As the ceiling over the stage exploded in a cascade of sparks, she took in the view of the crowd with amazement, even though she long ago sold out her first stadium.

It soon turned out that every song was its own mini-show. The impressive production techniques continued with Taylor grabbing a fluorescent, flashing drum to beat in the dark during the second song, the fan-favorite “[Holy Ground](https://taylorswiftswitzerland.ch/index.php/albums/red-album/red-songs/holy-ground/).” 12 other drummers leaped between floor and ceiling, bouncing on harnesses as they pounded along.

 Nobody could touch Taylor for fan hysteria, either. After darting around the stage for the first few minutes of the show, she made the first of a number of heartfelt speeches to her adoring crowd. “Hi, I’m Taylor,” she said by way of an introduction to the sound of thousands of screaming fans. “I write songs about my feelings. I’m told I have a lot of feelings.” She then gently warned the audience to “expect the unexpected” before topping off the opening segment with a rendition of “[Red](https://taylorswiftswitzerland.ch/index.php/albums/red-album/red-songs/red-song/),” complete with an impressive flag-waving gymnastic routine from her dancers. A quick costume change and she returned with her early hit “[You Belong With Me](https://taylorswiftswitzerland.ch/index.php/albums/fearless-album/fearless-songs/you-belong-with-me/)” before a set change to recall a bygone Hollywood era for “[The Lucky One](https://taylorswiftswitzerland.ch/index.php/albums/red-album/red-songs/the-lucky-one/).”

Through her eight wardrobe changes during the show, Taylor added many other set design changes, which was meant to take fans through the story of her songs. In fact, she spent quite a bit of time talking to the audience. Before “[Mean](https://taylorswiftswitzerland.ch/index.php/albums/speak-now-album/speak-now-songs/mean/)” she spoke about bullying and how she vowed to never be mean to anyone on purpose after she was treated poorly in school as a child. On a brighter note, she championed the good parts of a past relationship with an upbeat mashup of her own “[Stay Stay Stay](https://taylorswiftswitzerland.ch/index.php/albums/red-album/red-songs/stay-stay-stay/)“ and The Lumineers’ “Ho Hey.”

The mechanics of the show involved everyone. There was an inner pit, where fans could stand in between the catwalks which jutted out of the stage. Those seats were only made available to members of her official fan club, but Taylor also had a B-stage at the back of the floor seating area where she performed a few songs. Her most recent hit, “[22](https://taylorswiftswitzerland.ch/index.php/albums/red-album/red-songs/22-2/),” sent her around the side of the arena floor, through the screaming crowd, along with her dancers, to the small stage at the rear. She touched as many waving hands as she could along the way, singing all the while. It is a signature move of Taylor’s, to perform specially for the back of the stadium, and she exceeded expectations this time. Sitting on her sparkly red stool, playing acoustic guitar, the second stage rose high into the arena, and revolved, as she first sang a secret surprise song, then duetted with Ed Sheeran for “Everything Has Changed” and finally performed the ballad “[Begin Again](https://taylorswiftswitzerland.ch/index.php/albums/red-album/red-songs/begin-again/).” Then she launched into “[Sparks Fly](https://taylorswiftswitzerland.ch/index.php/albums/speak-now-album/speak-now-songs/sparks-fly/)” and flew over the audience back to the main stage just in time for more fireworks.

Her final five tracks provided even more highlights. Arguably the best moment of the night was the double-shot of “[I Knew You Were Trouble.](https://taylorswiftswitzerland.ch/index.php/albums/red-album/red-songs/i-knew-you-were-trouble/)” into “[All Too Well](https://taylorswiftswitzerland.ch/index.php/albums/red-album/red-songs/all-too-well/).” Taylor turned “Trouble” into a blast of razzle-dazzle choreography in fancy-dress masquerade-ball mode. Then she sat alone to play “All Too Well,” her most majestic ballad. “So this happened to me one time and I knew that in order to get past it I needed to write about it,” she said before the song. “So instead of trying to write how I felt about it, I just decided that it might be better to just write about what happened, because I remembered everything.” It was just her and her piano and several thousand other girls singing along. It was the highlight of a show that was nothing but highlights.

“[Love Story](https://taylorswiftswitzerland.ch/index.php/albums/fearless-album/fearless-songs/love-story/)” and “[Treacherous](https://taylorswiftswitzerland.ch/index.php/albums/red-album/red-songs/treacherous/)” followed, complete with a music box theme and an (almost) Cirque Du Soleil inspired routine with the dancers performing as wind-up ballerinas. Finally, the finale was truly outstanding. It was like Alice and Wonderland had wandered into a circus tent, with rabbits and stilt-walkers everywhere, and Taylor was their ring-leader in a red sequinned coat and top hat, clearly loving every sly moment of “[We Are Never Ever Getting Back Together](https://taylorswiftswitzerland.ch/index.php/albums/red-album/red-songs/we-are-never-ever-getting-back-together/).” The catwalk lifted up and spun her out across the audience, as heart-shaped red confetti canons exploded, and she led everyone in a deafening sing along, before saying thank you, good night, and disappearing back under the stage. There was no need for an encore — fans had already gotten everything they came for and more.

### Secret Song

 Every night, Taylor would sing a secret song — an acoustic version of one of her old songs. Fans could suggest songs online through Twitter and Facebook and Taylor would sing the most requested one. Sometimes she also performed a song that a fan from the pre-show Meet & Greet wanted to hear.

### Surprise Guests

 A fan of the concert cameo, Taylor welcomed many special surprise guests to her tour. Highlights include Carly Simon, who performed her classic hit “You’re So Vain” with Taylor at Gillette Stadium, Fall Out Boy, who appeared to sing “My Songs Know What You Did in the Dark,” and Jennifer Lopez, who brought the house down at Staples Center with “Jenny from the Block.”

### The RED Tour Movie

 The “Red Tour” remains Taylor’s only concert tour to never have been filmed. According to the CEO of her former label [Big Machine](https://taylorswiftswitzerland.ch/index.php/wiki/big-machine-records/), Scott Borchetta, he and the management never planned to film the concert or to put it on DVD. He said Taylor also never insisted to film “The RED Tour” due to her process of switching genres. Rumours online suggest that there was in fact a concert film in the works, but some serious allegations regarding the director got revealed at the time — which is why the project was permanently scrapped.

### Club RED

 Club RED was the name of the VIP backstage meet and greet for “The RED Tour.” As they did on Taylor’s previous tours, her mother, [Andrea Swift](https://taylorswiftswitzerland.ch/index.php/wiki/family/andrea-swift/), and members of [Taylor Nation](https://taylorswiftswitzerland.ch/index.php/wiki/13-management/) hand-picked fans that stood out the most during the concert: they had spent the entire concert screaming, crying, and bobbing mega-size [Meredith](https://taylorswiftswitzerland.ch/index.php/wiki/cats/meredith-grey/) cat heads in the crowd hoping to get picked by Taylor’s team to go to the exclusive event. The setup for Club RED included a bar, fridges stacked with [Diet Cokes](https://taylorswiftswitzerland.ch/index.php/wiki/brand-deals/diet-coke/) (a nod to the main sponsor of the tour), dining booths, sleek silver and red décor, a photobooth and lots of free food, including pizza. Once Taylor showed up, she would chat with every fan in the room, sign one of their belongings, and take a picture with them.

### Critical Reception

 “The RED Tour” received positive reviews from music critics, with many citing Taylor’s atmospheric performances as a specific area of praise. Writing for Rolling Stone, Rob Sheffield praised her “emotional excess [and] musical reach”, while Rebbeca Nicholson of The Guardian gave a 5-star review, stating Taylor was “staggeringly nice” and a “consummate crowd pleaser”. Digital Spy contributor Emma Dibdin stated the tour combined “whimsical spectacle with Swift’s trademark emotional intimacy,” and that it “capitalises on exactly what makes Swift such a powerful figure for her audience, the sincere blend of aspirational and relatable.”

### Records

 Taylor became the first solo female artist in 20 years to headline a national stadium tour through Australia, with the last being Madonna’s “The Girlie Show World Tour” in 1993. Taylor performed to a crowd of over 40,900 fans at the Allianz Stadium in Sydney, Australia, becoming the first female artist in history to sell out the stadium since it was opened in 1988.

“The RED Tour” also became the highest-grossing tour by a country artist in history, bringing in an overall gross of $150 million surpassing the prior country artist record held by double-billed Tim McGraw and Faith Hill “Soul2Soul II Tour” that brought in $141 million.

The Speak Now Tour (2011-2012)

Long live the walls we crashed through…

It was the second era, and basically the time in which Taylor was cementing herself from a one-album artist into an international phenomenon. The Speak Now album itself was also a transition, where every song was made by Taylor herself and hidden gems that didn’t made it into the mainstream media became fan favorites that only a few people would know. It remains Taylor’s most ambitious tour as well, taking her to countries she had never been before in Asia and Europe. We also get a new member and musical director: the immensely talented [David Cook](https://theswiftagency.com/profiles/david-cook/).

This was also the first tour that I covered from start to finish, writing entries for every city and came up with the label of Inside Speak Now whenever I was giving out spoilers for people who had not seen the tour yet. I wrote two personal concert experiences plus a rare treat: Meeting the Agency!

https://theswiftagency.com/wp-content/uploads/2010/11/taylor-swift-speak-now-tour-poster.jpg(Source: TaylorSwift.com)
The Speak Now Tour (2011-2012)

Long live the walls we crashed through…

It was the second era, and basically the time in which Taylor was cementing herself from a one-album artist into an international phenomenon. The Speak Now album itself was also a transition, where every song was made by Taylor herself and hidden gems that didn’t made it into the mainstream media became fan favorites that only a few people would know. It remains Taylor’s most ambitious tour as well, taking her to countries she had never been before in Asia and Europe. We also get a new member and musical director: the immensely talented [David Cook](https://theswiftagency.com/profiles/david-cook/).

This was also the first tour that I covered from start to finish, writing entries for every city and came up with the label of Inside Speak Now whenever I was giving out spoilers for people who had not seen the tour yet. I wrote two personal concert experiences plus a rare treat: Meeting the Agency!

- [Inside Speak Now: The Montreal Experience](https://theswiftagency.com/2011/07/15/inside-speak-now-the-montreal-experience/)

- [Inside Speak Now Nashville: The Main Event](https://theswiftagency.com/2011/09/20/speak-now-nashville/)

- [Meeting The Agency](https://theswiftagency.com/gallery/meeting-the-agency-2011-07-13/)

This tour also brought us the Arm Lyrics, surprise song covers usually relevant to the location where she was performing and duets with secret guests.

- [Speak Now Arm Lyrics](https://theswiftagency.com/extras/speak-now-arm-lyrics/)

Unlike previous tours focused on a single album release, ‘Taylor Swift: The Eras Tour’ is a monumental event taking fans on a journey through her incredible career. From the country twang of her debut to the pop perfection of “1989” and the alternative explorations of “folklore” and “evermore,” every era will have its moment to shine.

Are you ready to revisit your favorite albums and sing along to iconic hits? This comprehensive guide provides everything you need to know about the Taylor Swift Eras Tour in 2024, including confirmed dates, locations, and even some [travel tips](https://blog.tours4fun.com/)!

The Eras Tour commenced on March 17, 2023, in Glendale, [Arizona](https://www.tours4fun.com/sp/d-arizona/), United States. As of now, there are about 60 concerts remaining in 2024.

Currently, Taylor is gearing up for the European leg, with confirmed shows across major cities like Paris, [London](http://tours4fun.com/sp/d-london/), and Stockholm. Canada dates will follow in November and December, with stops in [Vancouver](https://www.tours4fun.com/sp/d-vancouver/) and Toronto (which is also the final show of the Eras Tour).

Here are the confirmed dates and locations for the upcoming Taylor Swift Eras Tour 2024:

Canada (November – December 2024)

Multiple eras, Multiple hits: The core concept of the tour – showcasing her music from different eras of her career – is a clear crowd-pleaser. Fans get to relive their favorite eras with elaborate stage designs and costume changes.

Deep cuts and fan favorites: Swift is reportedly mixing in fan-requested songs alongside the hits, making the setlist unpredictable and exciting for longtime fans.

Relatable moments: The recent release of the “Errors Tour” content within the “Taylor Swift: The Eras Tour Movie (Taylor’s Version)” shows her willingness to embrace imperfections. This adds a layer of relatability and humor to the live experience.

The list of Taylor Swift live performances chronicles the American singer-songwriter's extensive array of concerts, headlining tours, festival sets, award show appearances, television specials, benefit concerts, and other notable live events, spanning from her debut performances in 2006 through her record-shattering global tours in 2024.[[1]](#ref-1)
Swift's career in live music is defined by six major headlining concert tours that supported her studio albums and highlighted her artistic evolution from country roots to pop superstardom, alongside hundreds of one-off shows that amplified her cultural impact. The Fearless Tour (April 2009–July 2010) marked her first major arena outing, supporting her sophomore album Fearless and grossing approximately $66.5 million across 118 shows in North America.[[2]](#ref-2) The Speak Now World Tour (February 2011–March 2012) expanded internationally, earning $123.7 million from 110 performances across four continents while promoting her third album Speak Now.[[2]](#ref-2) Following suit, the Red Tour (March 2013–June 2014) grossed $150.2 million over 86 dates in 12 countries, blending country and pop elements from her album Red.[[3]](#ref-3) The 1989 World Tour (May–December 2015) fully embraced her pop transition, achieving $250 million in revenue from 85 shows worldwide and featuring high-profile guest appearances.[[4]](#ref-4) After a hiatus, the Reputation Stadium Tour (May–November 2018) set a then-record for U.S. tours by a female artist, grossing $345.7 million from 53 stadium dates across seven countries.[[5]](#ref-5) Culminating her touring legacy to date, The Eras Tour (March 2023–December 2024) became the highest-grossing concert tour in history, generating $2.077 billion in ticket sales from 149 sold-out shows attended by 10,168,008 fans in 21 countries across five continents, with each performance lasting over three hours and celebrating her entire discography.[[6]](#ref-6)[[7]](#ref-7)
Beyond tours, Swift's live performances encompass influential non-touring events, such as her breakthrough country festival appearances (e.g., at the 2007 [Country Music Association Awards](/page/Country_Music_Association_Awards)), pop-era award show spectacles (including Grammy performances in 2010 and 2021), benefit concerts like the 2011 *[Speak Now* World Tour Live](/page/Speak_Now_World_Tour_–_Live) recording, and high-profile integrations with sports events, such as the 2006 national anthem performance at the [Detroit Lions](/page/Detroit_Lions)' Thanksgiving game. These engagements, often featuring surprise guests and elaborate production, have solidified her status as one of the most dynamic live performers in modern music, contributing to economic boosts estimated in billions for host cities and influencing global fan culture through sold-out stadiums and viral moments.[[8]](#ref-8)[[9]](#ref-9)

## Concert tours

### Headlining tours

Taylor Swift has headlined numerous concert tours since the late 2000s, each supporting key albums in her discography and marking her progression from intimate theater and arena performances in her country roots to large-scale stadium productions in her pop era. These tours have collectively grossed billions of dollars, set attendance records, and featured evolving setlists that reflect her artistic growth, with special guests enhancing the live experience. Beginning with small-scale headlining efforts tied to her self-titled debut album, Swift's tours expanded internationally, emphasizing elaborate stage designs, costume changes, and fan engagement elements like surprise songs.
Her first major headlining tour, the [Fearless Tour](/page/Fearless_Tour) (2009–2010), supported her sophomore album Fearless and consisted of 118 shows primarily in arenas across [North America](/page/North_America), with extensions to [Europe](/page/Europe), [Asia](/page/Asia), and [Australia](/page/Australia). It grossed over $66.5 million and attracted more than 1.2 million attendees, featuring high-energy performances of hits like "[You Belong with Me](/page/You_Belong_with_Me)" and guest appearances from artists such as [John Mayer](/page/John_Mayer). The tour's success solidified Swift's status as a touring force, transitioning from theaters to larger venues.[[10]](#ref-10)[[11]](#ref-11)
The [Speak Now World Tour](/page/Speak_Now_World_Tour) (2011–2012) promoted [Speak Now](/page/Speak_Now) with 110 shows worldwide, including significant legs in [Asia](/page/Asia) and [Europe](/page/Europe), grossing $123.7 million. Known for its theatrical elements inspired by fairy-tale aesthetics, the tour featured solo performances early on before incorporating opening acts, and setlists focused on narrative-driven songs like "Enchanted." It marked Swift's first extensive international stadium dates, expanding her global fanbase.[[11]](#ref-11)
Supporting [Red](/page/Red), [the Red Tour](/page/The_Red_Tour) (2013–2014) ran for 86 shows across 12 countries, earning $150.2 million and emphasizing a mix of country and pop with special guests including [Ed Sheeran](/page/Ed_Sheeran) and [Gary Lightbody](/page/Gary_Lightbody) of [Snow Patrol](/page/Snow_Patrol). Venues shifted toward arenas and select stadiums, with setlists incorporating surprise covers and evolving to include more upbeat tracks, reflecting Swift's genre experimentation. This tour highlighted her ability to blend intimate moments with high-production spectacle.[[11]](#ref-11)
The [1989 World Tour](/page/The_1989_World_Tour) (2015), tied to her pop breakthrough album [1989](/page/1989), comprised 85 shows in stadiums and arenas globally, grossing $250.7 million and drawing record crowds, such as 75,980 at a [Sydney](/page/Sydney) performance. Featuring vibrant visuals, flying platforms, and guests like [Mick Jagger](/page/Mick_Jagger), the setlist celebrated synth-pop anthems like "[Shake It Off](/page/Shake_It_Off)" and marked Swift's full pivot to stadium-scale pop productions.[[11]](#ref-11)[[12]](#ref-12)
The [Reputation Stadium Tour](/page/Reputation_Stadium_Tour) (2018) supported [Reputation](/page/Reputation) with 53 all-stadium shows across [North America](/page/North_America) and [Europe](/page/Europe), grossing $345.7 million from 2.9 million tickets sold. Its dark, edgy theme included massive snake motifs and surprise guests like [Maren Morris](/page/Maren_Morris) for duets such as "The Middle," with setlists evolving to balance high-drama tracks with fan favorites. This tour underscored Swift's resilience post-media scrutiny, primarily in stadium venues.[[13]](#ref-13)[[14]](#ref-14)
Swift's most ambitious outing, [The Eras Tour](/page/The_Eras_Tour) (2023–2024), celebrated her entire catalog with 149 shows across five continents—[North America](/page/North_America), [South America](/page/South_America), [Europe](/page/Europe), [Asia](/page/Asia), and [Oceania](/page/Oceania)—grossing a record-breaking $2.077 billion from over 10 million tickets. Primarily in stadiums, it featured a three-hour setlist divided by album eras, with evolutions like additions from The Tortured Poets Department in 2024 and frequent surprise guests such as [Ice Spice](/page/Ice_Spice) and [Travis Scott](/page/Travis_Scott). The tour shattered attendance records, with multiple nights selling out instantly and generating unprecedented economic impact.[[15]](#ref-15)[[16]](#ref-16)

Swift's headlining [career](/page/Career) demonstrates a trajectory from country-flavored [arena](/page/Are.na) shows to pop-dominated global stadium events, with each tour breaking financial and attendance benchmarks while prioritizing fan interactivity and thematic innovation.[[17]](#ref-17)

### Promotional tours

Promotional tours consist of abbreviated concert series or mini-tours that Taylor Swift has used to generate buzz for new album releases, often limited to a handful of dates with setlists emphasizing unreleased or freshly debuted tracks to coincide with marketing campaigns and boost chart performance. These efforts differ from extended headlining tours by their focused, marketing-driven scope, typically involving fewer than 10 shows and integrating ticket sales with [pre-order](/page/Pre-order) incentives or merchandise bundles.[[18]](#ref-18)
In 2014, ahead of her album 1989, Swift conducted select promotional shows in the United States as part of an aggressive rollout strategy, including an outdoor concert on [Hollywood Boulevard](/page/Hollywood_Boulevard) for Jimmy Kimmel Live! on October 24, where she performed tracks like "[Shake It Off](/page/Shake_It_Off)" and "[Blank Space](/page/Blank_Space)" for the first time live, drawing massive crowds and contributing to the album's debut at No. 1 on the [Billboard 200](/page/Billboard_200) with over 1.28 million copies sold in its first week. Another key event was the CBS Radio's "The [1989](/page/1989) Experience" concert on October 25 in [Los Angeles](/page/Los_Angeles), featuring guest appearances by artists such as [Pharrell Williams](/page/Pharrell_Williams) and [Mary J. Blige](/page/Mary_J._Blige), with a setlist centered on 1989 material to heighten anticipation; these performances helped propel singles like "[Shake It Off](/page/Shake_It_Off)" to No. 1 on the [Billboard Hot 100](/page/Billboard_Hot_100) and solidified the album's pop transition.[[19]](#ref-19)[[20]](#ref-20)
The most prominent example of a dedicated promotional tour was Lover Fest in 2019, a festival-style mini-tour announced on September 17 to support her seventh studio album Lover, blending headline slots at existing events with standalone U.S. shows at venues like [SoFi Stadium](/page/SoFi_Stadium) in [Los Angeles](/page/Los_Angeles) (Lover Fest West) and [MetLife Stadium](/page/MetLife_Stadium) in East Rutherford (Lover Fest East), with tickets bundled to encourage album pre-orders. Originally comprising 13 dates across [Europe](/page/Europe), [Asia](/page/Asia), and [North America](/page/North_America), the tour emphasized intimate, colorful productions highlighting Lover's romantic themes, but the [COVID-19 pandemic](/page/COVID-19_pandemic) led to its cancellation in June 2020 after only three shows were completed: the [City of Lover](/page/City_of_Lover) concert on September 9, 2019, at L'Olympia in [Paris](/page/Paris), where Swift debuted five Lover tracks including "The Archer" and "Death by a Thousand Cuts" in an acoustic-heavy set for 2,000 fans; her set at the iHeartRadio Jingle Ball on December 6, 2019, in [Los Angeles](/page/Los_Angeles), featuring "Lover," "You Need to Calm Down," and the holiday single "Christmas Tree Farm"; and the Capital's Jingle Bell Ball on December 8, 2019, in [London](/page/London), with similar Lover-focused performances that reinforced the album's chart dominance, debuting at No. 1 on the Billboard 200. Despite the truncation, these events amplified Lover's commercial success, with the Paris show later released as the City of Lover Concert special in 2020.[[18]](#ref-18)[[21]](#ref-21)[[22]](#ref-22)
Earlier promotional efforts included one-off tie-ins like performances during the 2006 Tim McGraw Tour, where Swift opened for Tim McGraw and Faith Hill across North America, showcasing debut album singles such as "Tim McGraw" to promote her emerging career, helping the track reach No. 6 on the Billboard Hot Country Songs chart. In 2017, for Reputation, Swift opted for low-key surprise appearances, such as pop-up visits to fan listening parties in the U.S. following the album's November 10 release, where she performed acoustic snippets of tracks like "Look What You Made Me Do" to foster intimate hype amid her media blackout strategy, contributing to the album's 1.216 million first-week sales. During the 2020 pandemic, virtual performances served as extensions of promotional activities for surprise albums folklore and evermore, including the NPR Tiny Desk (Home) Concert in April 2020 featuring folklore songs like "The Lakes" and the Disney+ special Folklore: The Long Pond Studio Sessions in November 2020, which debuted evermore tracks in a stripped-down format streamed to millions and aiding both albums' No. 1 Billboard 200 debuts without traditional live tours.
As of November 2025, no major promotional tour has materialized for The Tortured Poets Department (2024), though Swift incorporated acoustic renditions of its tracks, such as "Fortnight" and "The Alchemy," into select dates of the ongoing [Eras Tour](/page/The_Eras_Tour) starting in May 2024, providing live debuts that supported the album's record-breaking 2.6 million first-week units while prioritizing the larger production.[[23]](#ref-23)

### Tours as opening act

Taylor Swift began her career as an opening act in 2006, supporting established country artists on their arena and amphitheater tours across the United States, which provided crucial exposure to large audiences during the promotion of her self-titled debut album.[[24]](#ref-24) These performances, spanning 2006 to 2009, helped her cultivate a dedicated country music fanbase before launching her first headlining tour in 2009.[[24]](#ref-24)
In 2007, Swift opened for George Strait on his Country Music Festival Tour, performing 17 shows from January 11 to March 3, primarily in U.S. arenas and coliseums such as the Cajundome in Lafayette, Louisiana, and KeyArena in Seattle, Washington.[[25]](#ref-25) Her setlists featured tracks from her debut album, including "Tim McGraw" and "Teardrops on My Guitar," which resonated with Strait's mature country audience and marked some of her earliest major-stage appearances. These gigs, drawing crowds of 10,000 to 15,000 per show, accelerated her visibility in the genre.[[26]](#ref-26)
That same year, she supported [Tim McGraw](/page/Tim_McGraw) and [Faith Hill](/page/Faith_Hill) on select dates of their [Soul2Soul II Tour](/page/Soul2Soul_II_Tour), totaling 10 performances between June and September across North American venues like the Air Canada Centre in [Toronto](/page/Toronto) and the MGM Grand Garden Arena in [Las Vegas](/page/Las_Vegas).[[27]](#ref-27) Swift's openings included songs like "Our Song" and "Picture to Burn," often earning praise from the headliners for her poise and songwriting talent, which McGraw later credited as spotting her star potential early.[[28]](#ref-28) The tour's high-profile status, with attendances exceeding 15,000 nightly, further solidified her rising profile in country circles.[[29]](#ref-29)
Swift continued as an opener for [Brad Paisley](/page/Brad_Paisley) on his Bonfires & Amplifiers Tour from October 2007 to early 2008, delivering 17 shows in U.S. amphitheaters and arenas, including the Verizon Wireless Amphitheater in [Charlotte, North Carolina](/page/Charlotte,_North_Carolina), and the CHI Health Center in [Omaha, Nebraska](/page/Omaha,_Nebraska).[[30]](#ref-30) Alongside openers like [Rodney Atkins](/page/Rodney_Atkins), she showcased an energetic set of debut-era hits such as "Should've Said No" and covers, adapting to Paisley's rock-infused country style and gaining traction with younger fans amid crowds of 12,000 to 20,000. This stint emphasized her versatility and contributed to the momentum leading into her sophomore album release.[[24]](#ref-24)
Her most extensive opening role came in 2008 on [Rascal Flatts](/page/Rascal_Flatts)' Bob That Head Tour, where she performed on 55 dates from June 13 to November 3, covering over 40 U.S. cities in arenas and amphitheaters like the [Resch Center](/page/Resch_Center) in [Ashwaubenon, Wisconsin](/page/Ashwaubenon,_Wisconsin), and the [Mohegan Sun Arena](/page/Mohegan_Sun_Arena) in [Uncasville, Connecticut](/page/Uncasville,_Connecticut).[[31]](#ref-31)[[32]](#ref-32) Setlists highlighted her growing catalog, including "Love Story" from her upcoming Fearless album alongside staples like "Our Song," debuting new material to enthusiastic responses from 15,000-plus attendees per show.[[33]](#ref-33) This tour, Rascal Flatts' largest to date, was pivotal in expanding her reach to mainstream country audiences and boosting album sales.[[24]](#ref-24)
In 2009, Swift opened for [Keith Urban](/page/Keith_Urban) on select dates of his Escape Together World Tour, appearing at 7 U.S. shows between June and August, such as Philips Arena in [Atlanta](/page/Atlanta) and TD Garden in [Boston](/page/Boston).[[34]](#ref-34) Her performances included a mix of Fearless tracks like "You Belong with Me" and fan favorites, with Urban later recalling her commanding presence and playful tour interactions, including pranks that highlighted her charisma.[[35]](#ref-35) These final opening slots, before her [Fearless Tour](/page/Fearless_Tour) headlining debut, drew 12,000 to 18,000 fans nightly and bridged her country roots to broader appeal.[[34]](#ref-34) After 2009, Swift did not serve as an opening act on any major tours, focusing instead on her own productions.[[24]](#ref-24)

## Non-tour live performances

### Festivals

Taylor Swift has performed at numerous music festivals throughout her career, often using these multi-artist events to promote her albums and showcase evolving musical styles from [country](/page/Country) to pop. Early appearances focused on U.S. festivals where she delivered intimate [country](/page/Country) sets, while later ones highlighted high-energy pop performances with surprise guests and elaborate productions. These festival slots, typically lasting 20-45 minutes, allowed her to connect with diverse crowds and experiment with setlists blending hits and new material.[[36]](#ref-36)
One of her earliest major festival outings was at [Lollapalooza](/page/Lollapalooza) in [Chicago](/page/Chicago) on August 2, 2008, where she performed on a side stage as a rising [country](/page/Country) artist, drawing crowds with songs from her self-titled debut album like "[Teardrops on My Guitar](/page/Teardrops_on_My_Guitar)" and "Our Song." The set emphasized her storytelling lyrics and acoustic elements, marking a pivotal moment in her transition from [opening act](/page/Opening_act) to festival draw amid a lineup featuring [Rage Against the Machine](/page/Rage_Against_the_Machine) and [Nine Inch Nails](/page/Nine_Inch_Nails).[[37]](#ref-37)
Swift headlined the [Austin City Limits Music Festival](/page/Austin_City_Limits_Music_Festival) in [Zilker Park](/page/Zilker_Park), Austin, for three consecutive years starting in 2008, adapting her setlists to reflect her growing catalog. In 2008 and 2009, performances included Fearless-era tracks such as "Love Story" and "[You Belong with Me](/page/You_Belong_with_Me)," performed to enthusiastic [Texas](/page/Texas) audiences and transitioning her from niche country appeal to broader pop crossover. By 2010, amid the [Speak Now](/page/Speak_Now) promotional cycle, she incorporated more theatrical elements, like costume changes, to sets featuring "Mine" and "Sparks Fly," solidifying her as a festival staple before shifting focus to full tours.[[38]](#ref-38)
Across the Atlantic, Swift made her mark at the Capital FM [Summertime Ball](/page/Summertime_Ball) in [London](/page/London), first appearing in 2009 at [Emirates Stadium](/page/Emirates_Stadium) with a set of upbeat country-pop hits that introduced her to [UK](/page/United_Kingdom) fans. She returned for headline slots in 2010 and 2011 at [Wembley Stadium](/page/Wembley_Stadium), performing medleys of "Fearless" and "[Speak Now](/page/Speak_Now)" tracks, often with acoustic twists to suit the event's pop-heavy vibe. In 2015, promoting [1989](/page/1989), she delivered a synth-pop set including "[Blank Space](/page/Blank_Space)" and "Style," joined by guests like [Vance Joy](/page/Vance_Joy) for collaborative moments that highlighted her genre evolution.[[39]](#ref-39)
The iHeartRadio Music Festival in Las Vegas provided key promotional platforms, with Swift closing the 2012 event at MGM Grand Garden Arena on September 22. Her setlist spanned "Sparks Fly," "Mean," and a debut of "We Are Never Ever Getting Back Together" from Red, blending country roots with emerging pop sensibilities to a star-studded crowd including Rihanna and Usher. She returned in 2014 for a surprise-heavy performance on September 20, opening with "Shake It Off" from her forthcoming 1989 album and incorporating viral dance moves that captured widespread media attention, emphasizing her shift to mainstream pop.[[40]](#ref-40)[[41]](#ref-41)
Jingle Ball events, organized by [iHeartRadio](/page/IHeartRadio) and other radio networks across U.S. cities, became annual holiday staples for Swift from 2007 onward, often serving as promotional tie-ins. Early sets in 2007-2009 at venues like [Madison Square Garden](/page/Madison_Square_Garden) featured acoustic holiday covers alongside "Picture to Burn" and "Love Story," fostering festive crowd sing-alongs. By the 2010s, performances evolved to include pop anthems; for instance, in 2014's KIIS-FM Jingle Ball in [Los Angeles](/page/Los_Angeles), she debuted "Out of the Woods," while 2017's tour across multiple cities spotlighted Reputation tracks like "Look What You Made Me Do" with dramatic lighting. The 2019 [iHeartRadio](/page/IHeartRadio) Jingle Ball in New York saw her perform Lover songs such as "ME!" and a live debut of "Christmas Tree Farm," mixing acoustics with full-band energy. She continued with appearances in 2022 and 2023, incorporating [Eras Tour](/page/The_Eras_Tour) elements like "Anti-Hero," but skipped the 2024 edition amid her focus on The Life of a Showgirl tour, with no confirmed 2025 slot as of November 2025. These events consistently drew massive reactions, with fans noting her ability to adapt elaborate productions to shorter formats.[[42]](#ref-42)
Regarding Glastonbury Festival, Swift was rumored for a 2010 slot but did not perform, and while offers circulated in the late 2010s, she was officially announced as the 2020 Pyramid Stage headliner on December 15, 2019, planning a Sunday night closing set. The event's cancellation due to the [COVID-19 pandemic](/page/COVID-19_pandemic) prevented the performance, and she has not returned to the festival since, prioritizing stadium tours over multi-day events post-2019. Guest appearances at other festivals, like a 2008 supporting slot at various U.S. radio festivals, further illustrated her early career trajectory, but her festival activity waned as her tours expanded globally.[[43]](#ref-43)

### Award shows

Taylor Swift has performed at numerous major award shows throughout her career, often using these platforms to showcase hits from her albums and occasionally collaborating with other artists. Her appearances have frequently coincided with nominations and wins, highlighting her evolution from [country](/page/Country) newcomer to global [pop icon](/page/Pop_icon). Notable moments include early [country](/page/Country) award triumphs and later high-profile pop spectacles, sometimes marked by controversies or special collaborations. These performances are typically broadcast [on television](/page/...on_Television) networks like ABC, [CBS](/page/CBS), or [MTV](/page/MTV), reaching millions of viewers.[[44]](#ref-44)
In 2007, Swift made her awards show debut performing "Tim McGraw" at the Academy of Country Music (ACM) Awards, where she met the song's namesake artist backstage, marking a pivotal early career moment.[[45]](#ref-45) Later that year at the [Country Music Association](/page/Country_Music_Association) (CMA) Awards, she delivered "Our Song," her first No. 1 country hit, and won the Horizon Award as the youngest recipient at age 17.[[46]](#ref-46) In [2008](/page/2008), she returned to the CMA Awards with "Love Story," the lead single from her sophomore album Fearless, which helped propel the record to massive success.[[47]](#ref-47) At the 2008 ACM Awards, Swift performed "Should've Said No," earning the Top New Female Vocalist award and solidifying her rising status in country music.[[48]](#ref-48)
Swift's ACM appearances continued in subsequent years; she performed multiple times between 2009 and 2011, including "You Belong with Me" in 2009 amid nominations for Fearless, and returned in 2011 as Entertainer of the Year winner, performing tracks from Speak Now.[[49]](#ref-49) At the 2009 MTV Video Music Awards (VMAs), her rendition of "You Belong with Me" was famously interrupted by Kanye West's onstage remark, a moment that drew widespread media attention and boosted the song's visibility, though she won Best Female Video that night.[[50]](#ref-50) In 2010, at the Grammy Awards, Swift joined Stevie Nicks for a duet of "You Belong with Me" followed by Nicks' "Rhiannon," earning praise for the intergenerational collaboration during her Best Country Album win for Fearless.[[51]](#ref-51)
The [American Music Awards](/page/American_Music_Awards) (AMAs) became a staple for Swift starting in 2009, where she performed "Love Story" and "Fearless," sweeping eight awards including [Artist of the Year](/page/Artist_of_the_Year). She continued with multiple appearances through 2022, such as "[Midnight Rain](/page/Midnight_Rain)" in 2022 from [Midnight](/page/Midnight), often tying performances to album promotions and record wins, amassing 40 AMAs overall.[[44]](#ref-44) At the 2013 VMAs, Swift debuted "[I Knew You Were Trouble](/page/I_Knew_You_Were_Trouble)" in a theatrical setup, winning Video of the Year for "We Are Never Ever Getting Back Together." She did not perform at the 2023 VMAs but accepted multiple awards.[[50]](#ref-50)
In 2015, Swift presented a medley at the Grammys featuring "Blank Space" from [1989](/page/1989), which won Album of the Year, showcasing her pop transition with high-energy choreography.[[51]](#ref-51) The Billboard Music Awards saw her from 2011 to 2019, including a 2011 performance of "Sparks Fly" amid [Speak Now](/page/Speak_Now) promotions and a 2019 medley of "ME!" with [Brendon Urie](/page/Brendon_Urie), aligning with her 23 wins in the ceremony's history.[[52]](#ref-52)
More recently, Swift attended the 2024 VMAs without performing but won Video of the Year for "[Fortnight](/page/Fortnight)" featuring [Post Malone](/page/Post_Malone). At the 2025 Grammys, she was present for nominations including Album of the Year for The [Tortured](/page/The_Tortured) Poets Department but did not perform, instead notably dancing in the audience during other acts.[[53]](#ref-53)[[54]](#ref-54) For the 2025 iHeartRadio [Music](/page/Music) Awards, Swift accepted the Tour of the Century award for her [Eras Tour](/page/The_Eras_Tour) via video message but did not perform live, having received nine nominations that year.[[55]](#ref-55)
